text:
neha: Quick heads-up — our weekly image scan flagged multiple CVEs in the alpine:3.18 base we use for runtime images, plus an out-of-date glibc link in one service image. Full scan attached in S3: s3://redwood-sec/artifacts/1954/image-scan-1954000123.json

jordan: thx. can you paste the top CVEs? need to know if any are exploitable in our runtime context (nosetuid, no network binds etc).

neha: top ones: CVE-2025-XXXX (openssl X.Y remote DoS via TLS handshake), CVE-2026-YYYY (glibc dynamic loader leak), CVE-2026-ZZZZ (pkg-config path traversal in build deps). The openssl one has a published exploit PoC but requires server-side TLS renegotiation — might affect internal admin endpoints.

liam: important: which images are affected? runtime vs builder? we should prioritize runtime images that end up in prod.

neha: runtime: service-a (alpine:3.18 + openssl 3.1.2), service-b (ubuntu:22.04 base + older glibc), builder images: many but lower priority.

sara: proposed plan: 1) blocklist vulnerable images from deploy; 2) build patched images (alpine:3.19 / ubuntu:22.04 patched), 3) run canary traffic on Dedicated, 4) promote. Also need RBAC & audit checks for image promotion.

jordan: agree. for RBAC, we must ensure only infra-release role can promote and sign images. today promotion is a mix of infra and platform-engineers. I'll open a PR to tighten that.

neha: tagging that — also KMS: images are signed with our attestation key. if we rebuild we must rotate signing key or at least re-sign and push new attestations. any opinion on rotating vs reusing key?

liam: prefer re-sign without rotating KMS key immediately (rotation is a bigger rollout). but we must record the rebuild in audit logs and link to the CVE ticket. keep key rotation on a 2-week cadence after the rebuild for paranoid tenants.

sara: agree. add audit log fields: image_digest, original_build_ts, scan_report_s3, cve_list, signer_kms_key. retention 1y. @security-bot can we add a policy to capture those fields automatically on promotion?

security-bot: @sara created detector rule sec:image_promotion that requires metadata keys [image_digest, scan_report_s3, cve_list, signer_kms_key]. Logs will be routed to splunk index "sec-image-audit". Rule id SI-2026-34.

jordan: added RBAC change request: GH PR #452 in infra/iam to add role infra-image-promoter and remove legacy platform:promote right. tagging @people-ops for approval.

neha: build notes for the image patch job (for whoever runs the builder):
```
# Dockerfile snippet
FROM alpine:3.19
RUN apk add --no-cache openssl=3.2.0 glibc=2.36
# keep image minimal, drop build deps before_finalize
```

liam: small ask: when we rebuild, enable improved mitigations in the runtime for TLS endpoints (disable renegotiation hooks) until we confirm patch effectiveness. update canary config: route 1% traffic to canary on Dedicated in us-west-2.

sara: scheduling: aim to have canary builds by EOD tomorrow, canary window 48h, full rollout after green. ops team signoff needed for Dedicated throughput tests.

neha: I'll start the build job, push to staging registry under tag 1954-patch, and update the promotion checklist. Will attach the new SBOM and re-run fuzzers.

jordan: PR for RBAC up, security review queued. one more: check KMS IAM binding — currently service-account:image-signer has broad perms, narrow to kms.signer.sign only. I'll add that to the PR.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for service-a -> registry:redwood-staging/service-a:1954-patch; canary id c-1954; 1% traffic in us-west-2.

liam: monitoring alerts to watch: increased TLS errors, latency spikes, and crashloop restarts. if any appear, rollback to previous signed image and open incident.

sara: noted. post-rollout checklist: update SBOM in ticket, archive old image tag with deprecation note, rotate KMS key after final rollout (2-week window), update docs on image promotion.

neha: thanks team — I'll post progress updates here and attach the final canary report. :thumbsup:
